turns.doctor_question: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to the clinic?
turns.patient_response:
Hello, Doctor. Well, I suppose what brings me in is that my wife thinks I'm not eating enough. She's the one who pushed for this appointment. 

Honestly, most days I just have some coffee and a piece of toast in the morning... and then maybe a little soup or some vegetables later on. I just feel like big meals are pretty unnecessary at my age. But she was worried about it, so here I am.

symptom_reasoning.S043: The patient describes eating very small amounts of food daily, consisting only of coffee, toast, and a little soup or vegetables, which demonstrates restrictive intake.

turns.doctor_question: When you're not eating much, is it because you're just not feeling hungry, or is it more that you're choosing not to eat even when you feel hungry?
turns.patient_response:
Well, I do feel hungry sometimes. It's not that my appetite is completely gone. It's more that... I guess I choose to hold back. 

You see, when my wife tries to put butter on things, or if she serves me a big, full plate of food, I just get nervous. I worry that I'll start putting weight back on if I eat all that. I've worked hard to keep a certain amount of control over my weight, and I really don't want to lose that control. So, I just stick to my smaller portions, even if my stomach is rumbling a bit.

symptom_reasoning.S045: The patient explicitly confirms an intense fear of gaining weight and anxiety over losing control of their weight, leading them to deliberately restrict portions.

turns.doctor_question: When you look at yourself in the mirror or think about your body, do you feel like you're overweight or at risk of becoming overweight, even if others might say you look thin?
turns.patient_response:
Well, I wouldn't say I look at myself and think I'm completely overweight, but... I do pay close attention to my shape. 

It's more about how things fit and feel. Like, if my belt feels a notch looser, I feel like I've done right by myself. It means I'm keeping things in check. But if I look in the mirror and my stomach looks the least bit rounded... well, I just feel sloppy and disappointed in myself. I don't want to get soft or lose the discipline I've kept up, you know? So I guess I do worry about becoming overweight, even if my wife says I'm too thin.

symptom_reasoning.S046: The patient describes how their self-esteem and feelings of self-worth ('done right by myself' vs. 'sloppy and disappointed in myself') are heavily contingent on subtle aspects of their body shape and clothing fit, reflecting an undue influence of shape and weight on self-evaluation.

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever had episodes where you felt like you lost control and ate a large amount of food in a short period of time? And if so, have you ever done anything to try to undo that eating, like making yourself vomit, exercising excessively, or using laxatives?
turns.patient_response:
No, I can't say I've ever done that. I don't lose control and eat large amounts of food... it's really the exact opposite for me. 

And I definitely don't make myself throw up or take laxatives or anything like that. I don't go crazy with exercise either—my knees wouldn't exactly allow that at my age anyway. I just... I just keep my portions very small from the start, so there's never really anything I feel the need to undo.

symptom_reasoning.S043: The patient confirms restricting intake by keeping their food portions very small from the start.
symptom_reasoning.S047: The patient explicitly denies engaging in compensatory behaviors such as excessive exercise to undo eating.
symptom_reasoning.S048: The patient explicitly denies purging behaviors, stating they never make themselves vomit or use laxatives.
symptom_reasoning.S049: The patient explicitly denies eating large amounts of food, stating they have never done that.
symptom_reasoning.S050: The patient explicitly denies having episodes where they lose control over eating.

turns.doctor_question: What is your current weight, and roughly how tall are you? I'd also like to know if your weight has changed significantly over the past year or two.
turns.patient_response:
Well, I'm about five foot ten. And right now, I weigh right around 135 pounds. 

It has gone down over the last year or two, yes. My regular doctor actually told me recently that the number on the scale has gotten too low. But honestly, to me... being lighter just makes it a lot easier to get around. It's much better for my joints when I'm working out in the garden, and it helps me keep up on my daily walks without feeling dragged down. So I don't really see the lower weight as a bad thing.

symptom_reasoning.S044: The patient reports a decrease in weight to 135 pounds at 5'10", confirms their physician noted their weight has gotten too low, and expresses an insistence on maintaining or viewing this lower weight positively.

turns.doctor_question: Based on your height of five foot ten and weight of 135 pounds, that gives you a BMI of about 19.4. Has your weight ever dropped below 120 pounds, which would put you closer to an underweight BMI?
turns.patient_response: No, I don't believe it's ever gotten quite that low. I usually hover right around the 135 mark. I check the scale most mornings, and it's been pretty steady there for a while now. I haven't seen it drop down into the 120s or below.

symptom_reasoning.S044: The patient explicitly denies ever dropping below 120 pounds and reports maintaining a steady weight around 135 pounds (normal BMI), denying significantly low body weight.

turns.doctor_question: How long have you been restricting your food intake and maintaining these smaller portions? Has this pattern of eating been going on for several months, or longer than that?
turns.patient_response: Well, it's been quite a while now. I'd say it's definitely been going on for longer than just a few months. I've been eating these smaller portions for... probably a couple of years, actually. It's just become my normal routine at this point.

symptom_reasoning.S043: The patient confirms persistently eating smaller portions as their normal routine for a couple of years, reflecting restrictive food intake.

turns.doctor_question: You mentioned your weight has been around 135 pounds for a while now. What was your weight at its lowest point during these past couple of years when you've been restricting your food intake?
turns.patient_response: Well, like I said, it hasn't ever dropped below 120. I think the absolute lowest I've seen on the scale over the last couple of years was maybe... 130? 132? Something right around there. It really just stays pretty close to 135 most of the time.

turns.doctor_question: When your weight was at its lowest point around 130 to 132 pounds, did your doctor or anyone else express concern that you were underweight, or did you notice any physical changes like feeling cold easily, your hair thinning, or irregular periods?
turns.patient_response: Well, my doctor has mentioned a few times that the number on the scale has gotten too low. He seems a bit concerned about it. But honestly, to me, being a little lighter just makes it easier to get around. I spend a lot of time in my garden, and I try to keep up with my daily walks, and carrying less weight around just makes all of that much easier on my joints. I haven't really noticed any of those other things you mentioned, like feeling cold or hair thinning. I just feel like it's easier to move.

symptom_reasoning.S044: The patient confirms that their doctor has repeatedly expressed concern that their weight is too low, acknowledging having a significantly low weight.
